27.0.0.en: His eyes were dim: his eyes were weary, that is, he had almost lost his sight.

27.0.1.en: Your quiver: the pouch or case in which the arrows are placed.

27.0.2.en: Isaac advanced in age and reached about 130 years, so he summoned his firstborn son Esau and said to him, I am old and the day of my death is near, so go and hunt an animal and prepare it as food for me, that you may show your love toward me, and I will eat and give you the blessing of the birthright before I depart from this life.

27.0.3.en: Although Isaac knew God's word that the elder would serve the younger, and had heard that Esau had sold his birthright for a meal of lentils to his brother Jacob, and was also troubled by his marriage to the wicked daughters of Heth, his fatherhood and his love for Esau moved him to give him the blessing, since he was the firstborn. Isaac could have been more self-restrained and blessed him without asking for food; rather, it would have been more fitting for him to pray first and seek God's guidance before proceeding to give the blessing to Esau.

27.0.4.en: It is good that you give gifts and help to your children and all those around you, but you need to pray first so that God may guide you, so as not to distress anyone while you are giving to another, and so that you may be just and doing God's will, meet the needs of those most in need and show love to all. Then you will not be troubled by opposing opinions, since you have no personal aim except carrying out God's will.

27.1.0.en: Rebekah was standing near Isaac when he spoke to his son Esau to prepare food for him and bring it to him, and she saw that Esau had gone out to hunt game and present it to his father.

27.2.0.en: Rebekah called her son Jacob and told him what Isaac had said to Esau, that is, that he should bring him food to eat, and then he would bless him.

27.3.0.en: She gave her son Jacob the advice that he should hasten to slaughter two kids from his flock and bring them to her, and she would prepare from them the foods that she knew his father loved, and he would go in with them to his father and pretend that he was Esau and take the blessing instead of him. Although Jacob was a perfect man living a life of righteousness and deserved the blessing according to God's promise, it was not right for Rebekah to use wrong methods to reach the blessing, but she should have left it to God, believing that He was able to give him the blessing in a sound way.

27.4.0.en: Jacob agreed in principle to the lying and the deceiving of his father, but he presented to his mother a problem, namely that his brother was hairy and he was smooth, so if his father touched him he would discover his deceit and be angry with him and curse him, and he would receive not a blessing but a curse.

27.5.0.en: Rebekah said to her son, Do not fear your father's curse, for it is on me. This is a strange saying without meaning, because a curse is not transferred from one person to another, but it is an attempt by the mother to encourage her son to the sin of deceit, and she considered the matter hers and not her son's, so she said to him, Fetch me two kids, and not, Fetch yourself two kids.

27.5.1.en: However good your aim may be, be careful in choosing the right means, and beware of encouraging another to sin, lest you and he fall into it, because all material gains are worthless in comparison with disobeying God.

27.6.0.en: Jacob brought the two kids to his mother, and she prepared from them many dishes of the kind Isaac loved.

27.7.0.en: Rebekah brought some of Esau's clothes that were in the big house, not those at his wives' homes, and put them on Jacob. Usually a person's smell, that is, the smell of his sweat together with the pleasant scents he is accustomed to using, is apparent in his clothes, so that if Isaac smelled him he would not doubt. She put goatskins on Jacob's hands and on his neck, so he became hairy like his brother Esau, and he took the food and went in to his father and called to him.

27.8.0.en: Jacob said to his father, I am Esau your son; arise, eat of my game and bless me. Isaac wondered at the speed of Esau's coming and said to him, How were you able to hunt and cook the food so quickly? Jacob said to him, Your God made everything easy for me. This was a spiritual answer that Esau was not accustomed to giving because of his distance from God, which increased Isaac's doubt.

27.9.0.en: Isaac asked his son to come near to him and touched his hands and found them hairy, and said, The voice is Jacob's voice, but the feel of the hands appears to be Esau's, because the voices of twins, however close, and however much one tries to imitate the other, will have a difference. Then he asked him again to make sure that he was his son Esau, and Jacob answered, Yes. Isaac found nothing before him but to ask for the food and eat, and then he drank wine.

27.10.0.en: After he had eaten, he wanted to make sure one last time, so he asked his son to come near to him and kiss him as a sign of showing love, but in truth he wanted to smell him, and he found the smell to be Esau's, because Jacob was wearing the clothes of his brother Esau. Then Isaac pronounced the blessing and said that the smell of his son was like the smell of a field that the Lord had blessed, and wished him fields that would give many crops with a fragrant smell by God's blessing.

27.11.0.en: He also asked for him a blessing from heaven, namely the dew and the rains to water his crops, and likewise he asked God for him fertility in the earth to make his crops grow, and then asked for him abundance of corn and grain, and also wine, by which is meant all the fruits of the earth. The word wine here in the original also means fresh wine, that is, the fruits of the earth and not fermented grape juice.

27.12.0.en: He also gave him the blessing that he would rule over his brothers and have dominion over many peoples, and everyone who loved and blessed him would receive a blessing from God, while whoever opposed and cursed him, God would curse him, that is, he would lose every blessing. These blessings are material, and Jacob received them at different times, such as God's blessing on his flocks with Laban, God's blessing on his possessions when he returned to Canaan, and the good things he received in Egypt in the days of Joseph, in addition to his offspring's taking possession of the Promised Land. But with these blessings he also met tribulations, so that God might raise us to the spiritual blessing, which is the most important, with the coming of Christ from his offspring, who offers salvation and blessing to the whole world, and the world is made subject (to Christ) through faith.

27.12.1.en: Thus Jacob received the blessing, but he fell into the sins of stealing, lying and deceit.

27.13.s.en: (3) Esau is deprived of the blessing

27.13.0.en: After Jacob had received the blessing from his father Isaac and departed, Esau arrived with his game and prepared his food, and went in to his father and asked him to arise and eat.

27.14.0.en: Isaac asked him, Who are you? and he answered that he was his son Esau. Isaac was agitated and troubled and asked, Who is it who came to me and told me that he was Esau, so that I ate of his food and blessed him? And he will indeed be blessed, and the blessing will not be taken away from him.

27.15.0.en: Esau grieved at this unfortunate surprise, for he had lost his blessing, so he cried out with a great voice to express his unbearable distress. Then Isaac answered him sorrowfully that Jacob had come and stolen the blessing. Esau was enraged and said that it was Jacob who had supplanted him and taken his birthright, and now for the second time he had taken his blessing; then he asked his father to give him some blessing. Sadly, Esau's concern was for the material blessing only and not the spiritual, and he did not regret in his heart his despising of the birthright, nor did he repent before God, but all his concern was in obtaining material things.

27.16.0.en: Isaac said to Esau, Jacob has taken the whole blessing, for he has received dominion over his brothers and the material blessings of the fruits of the earth, expressed by the corn and wine.

27.17.0.en: Esau said to his father, Have you but one blessing? ... Bless me, even me also, and he wept; but this was not the weeping of repentance but grief at the loss of material things, and of course he had no thought of the spiritual blessing, which is indeed one, because it is fulfilled in Christ, who comes from the offspring of Jacob.

27.18.0.en: Isaac assured Esau that he would be without the blessing, so he would not receive blessings from heaven, expressed by the dew, nor from the earth, that is, its fertility.

27.19.0.en: By your sword you shall live: he will enter into many wars.

27.19.1.en: Have the dominion: the disobedience of an animal toward the one who leads it, meaning the revolt and rebellion of the offspring of Esau against the offspring of Jacob.

27.19.2.en: His yoke: the crosspiece of wood placed on the necks of the animals that pull agricultural implements, meaning the rejection of the dominion of the offspring of Jacob over him.

27.19.3.en: He also prophesied to Esau that he would be fierce, inclined to war, and that his brother Jacob would have dominion over him, but that he would sometimes revolt against Jacob and prevail over him. The offspring of Jacob took possession of the land of Canaan and Edom, the offspring of Esau, was subject to them, but at times it rebelled and fought the people of Israel.

27.19.4.en: Do not despise the blessing when it is available to you, lest you ask for it at another time and not find it, and do not despise the opportunity of a lifetime for repentance before the day of judgment comes and all opportunities are lost to you.

27.20.0.en: Esau bore a grudge against his brother Jacob because he had received all the blessings while he was deprived of them, and because his thinking was entirely material he thought in a human way, namely to kill him so that he himself would receive all the blessings, not knowing that the blessings are spiritual in essence and are from God, before whom he cannot stand or whom he cannot oppose. But God put it in his heart to fear his father Isaac, so he postponed the matter until Isaac should die and his mourning, that is, his funeral, be completed, and then kill his brother.

27.21.0.en: Comforting himself: he calms himself temporarily concerning you until a suitable time comes in which to kill you.

27.21.1.en: Rebekah heard of Esau's resolve to kill his brother, so she told Jacob of this and advised him to flee to her brother Laban in Haran, which is between the two rivers in Iraq, and to stay there a short while until Esau's anger subsided, and then she would send and fetch him.

27.22.0.en: On the other hand, she told Isaac how distressed she was by Esau's pagan wives, the daughters of Heth, and her fear that Jacob would take a wife from among them, and her wish that he would marry from the daughters of her people. Isaac agreed, who had begun to feel the fulfillment of God's word and Jacob's right to the blessing.

27.22.1.en: Rebekah carried out what she and Jacob wanted, but she lost the presence of her son beside her and the distress of her other son with her and with his brother. As for Jacob, he bore much suffering, whether from Laban his uncle, or from his sons when they killed the men of Shechem, or his loss of Joseph ... all this God permitted as discipline for repentance. As for Rebekah, she is not mentioned in the Holy Bible after that, so it is understood that she died before Jacob returned to Canaan after 20 years, without seeing him.

27.22.2.en: Do not rush toward material gains or to carry out your will, however good it may seem, and seek God before every deed and think well, so that Satan does not exploit your impulsiveness and make you fall into sins foreign to you.

27.22.3.en: Here we summarize the life of Isaac as the Holy Bible relates it, as follows:

27.22.4.en: 1- The birth of Isaac, the son of the promise (ch. 21)

27.22.5.en: 2- The offering of Isaac as a sacrifice (ch. 22)

27.22.6.en: 3- The choosing of Rebekah as a wife for Isaac (ch. 24)

27.22.8.en: 5- Isaac's sojourn in Gerar and his digging out of the wells of water (ch. 26)

27.22.9.en: 6- Jacob steals the blessing from Isaac (ch. 27)

27.22.10.en: 7- The death of Isaac (ch. 35) Jacob's ladder

28.0.0.en: Isaac summoned his son Jacob to bid him farewell and give him a parting charge before his journey. This shows Isaac's love for Jacob and his faith that the divine promises were being fulfilled in him, so he said to him, Do not marry any of the pagan, wicked Canaanite women among whom you live.

28.1.0.en: He also charged him to travel to the region of Padan-aram, which lies between the two rivers in the north, where his mother's family lives, his grandfather Bethuel and his uncle Laban, and to take a wife for himself from the daughters of his uncle.

28.2.0.en: He asked for Jacob that God would bless him with many offspring, and that his offspring would be a blessing to all peoples. This was fulfilled not in the people of Israel as a people proclaiming faith in God among the pagans, but rather in Christ, who offers salvation and blessing to the whole world.

28.3.0.en: He wished for him the fulfillment of God's promises to Abraham of the inheritance of the land of Canaan and the possession of it.

28.4.0.en: After that Jacob departed and traveled on his way from Canaan to Haran, where his uncle Laban lived.

28.4.1.en: Care for the advice of your parents and those responsible for you, for it is a message from God that helps you to a life of righteousness, so that you are joined to God and live uprightly.

28.5.0.en: Jacob went on his way from Beersheba in the south of Canaan, the land of the Philistines, to Haran, which lies in the north of Iraq, where his uncle Laban lived (map 8). After he had grown weary walking all day, he rested in a secluded place in the desert, because the sun had set and it was not possible to travel at night. He felt fear of being pursued by his brother Esau, who could kill him, and he also felt loneliness and estrangement in the wilderness and the loss of his parents' care and his well-equipped tent. From weariness he slept on the ground, and took a stone and made it a pillow for his head and slept there in this extreme poverty, and nothing remained to him but his faith in God. This stone is a type of Christ, the cornerstone on which we build all our life.

28.5.1.en: When things grow narrow for you and you lose much of what you lean on of material things and human relationships, know that God is then nearest to you, so seek Him and lean on Him, and you will find your rest.

28.6.0.en: He saw in a dream a ladder rising from the earth to heaven, and angels ascending and descending on it.

28.6.1.en: This ladder is a type of the Cross of Christ, on which the angels ascend, praising God for His redemption of mankind, and descend from it to proclaim the glad tidings of Christ the Redeemer to the world so that they may believe in Him. By this ladder, that is, the Cross, believers are raised to heaven, while those who reject it go down to Hades.

28.6.2.en: The ladder is also a type of the Virgin Mary, through whose Son we are raised to heaven and proclaim His name to the world.

28.7.0.en: Jacob heard the voice of God from above the ladder, who declared to him that He was the God of Abraham and Isaac his fathers, who had given them the promises, and now He was confirming His promise with him also, that He would give him the land on which he lay. He means the whole land of Canaan as He promised Abraham, and He would bless his offspring so that it would be very many like the dust of the earth, and keep him on his way to his uncle and bring him back to his land and never leave him, and in his offspring all the peoples of the earth would be blessed, that is, in Christ who comes from his offspring.

28.7.1.en: The meaning of until at the end of (v. 15) is not a particular time after which God would leave him, but that He would not leave him throughout his life and would fulfill all His promises to him.

28.8.0.en: When Jacob awoke from his sleep he was sure that this dream was a true revelation from God and that God was with him in this place, so he felt reverence, holiness and joy before Him, and declared that since God was in this place, it was His house, because the house of God is the place of His meeting with man, indeed it is the gate of heaven. This is the first clear reference to the Church, the house of God.

28.9.0.en: Jacob took the stone on which he had slept and set it up as a pillar and poured oil on it.

28.9.1.en: The stone, as we mentioned, is a type of Christ, the Rock of ages, and the oil is a type of the Holy Spirit, and the pouring of the oil means the consecration of the stone and the place, declaring that it is the place of God. He called the place Bethel, that is, the house of God, while the city near this place, which was called Bethel, was formerly called Luz because of the abundance of almond trees in it.

28.10.0.en: In view of God's care for Jacob and His appearing to him on the ladder, Jacob promised that if God kept him on his way to Haran and brought him back to the land of Canaan in which he had been living, and provided for his needs of food and clothing, he would do three things:

28.10.1.en: 1- That he would continue to worship God throughout his life. The importance of this matter appears because Jacob and his father and mother were the only ones in the whole world at that time who worshiped God.

28.10.2.en: 2- That he would build an altar to God in this place, and Bethel would become God's place for His worship.

28.10.3.en: 3- That he would give God a tenth of the possessions that He gave him.

28.10.4.en: How beautiful it is that you make promises to God on every occasion, so that you may live with Him and be joined to Him by various spiritual means, which encourage you to spiritual growth.

28.10.5.en: Jacob's marriage to Leah and Rachel
